chapter: Jazz opinions, Jelly Roll and the Rhythm Club
title: Church attitudes toward jazz
summary: Church people objected to jazzing church tunes; Saints Go Marching In was the biggest.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: How did the church people look upon jazz music?

They didn't in the beginning because I remember when my sister was going to Atlanta University and they made a jazz tune out of some church tune and the president made some kind of speech about it. I was over there.
I don't even know the name of it, but the first religious tune, the biggest hit was When the Saints Come Marching Home. That's the only one I remember.
They didn't want you to play jazz?
No, they didn't want it then.
They didn't want you to dance?
No, they didn't mind you dancing but they just didn't like to hear church tunes, you know....
They didn't want you to jazz up the spirituals?
But they didn't mind the other?
No, play anything you want, dance. The "Saint" thing is the biggest thing that ever happened yet, in my knowledge.
